mainTopic: How נדרים and שבועות differ: when an oath is stricter, and why a vow but not an oath can override a מצוה
overview: The גמרא first asks how the משנה can call something 'a stringency of oaths over vows' when the vow version had no effect at all. It answers that the משנה is pointing to a different case: an oath not to sleep, speak or walk. Next it turns to the opposite rule, that vows can be stricter than oaths. רב גידל, quoting רב or שמואל, learns from 'לא יחל דברו' that a person cannot swear to break the מצוות. The גמרא then challenges this, because the same פסוק talks about both נדר and שבועה. אביי answers that the difference is in the wording: 'the benefit of a סוכה is forbidden to me' versus 'I swear not to benefit from the סוכה.' רבא objects that doing a מצוה is not 'benefit', so he uses 'sitting in a סוכה' instead. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the rule against swearing to break מצוות really comes from this פסוק. It begins quoting a ברייתא as the other source, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can it be a 'stringency' if the vow did nothing?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'חומר' (stringency) suggests the vow is a real vow, just weaker. But the משנה said the vow case is 'permitted', meaning it did nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה says 'a stringency.' That implies the vow is still a vow, just a weaker one. But the משנה taught that in the vow case he is 'permitted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging the wording of the משנה. Calling the oath 'stricter' seems to clash with what the משנה said about the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Stricter' usually means both things work, and one simply works more strongly. But the משנה ruled that with vow wording the person is fully permitted, so the vow seems to have done nothing. If the vow does nothing, calling the oath 'stricter' is the wrong way to describe it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
By implication; we can infer from this
But look, doesn't it...? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: GEMARA: "A stringency,"
this implies that it is a vow.
But it teaches "permitted"!
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier case in the משנה where, with vow wording, he is allowed to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'זה חומר בשבועות מבנדרים'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Stricter' implies the vow works, only more weakly. Yet the משנה said the vow case is completely permitted.

steps.title: The stringency refers to the oath not to sleep, speak or walk
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's 'stringency' line is attached to a different case: an oath not to sleep, speak or walk, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught about the end of the other section: 'An oath that I will not sleep,' 'that I will not speak,' 'that I will not walk': it is forbidden. That is the case where the oath is stricter than the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'stringency' line does not refer to the eating case. It refers to the other section, about sleeping, speaking and walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sleeping, speaking and walking cases, a vow is weaker, because those are actions and not objects. Yet the vow there is not simply 'permitted'. An oath on those same actions fully binds him. So comparing those two, it is correct to say the oath is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause; the end part

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'oaths are stricter than vows' line refers to oaths on actions like sleeping, speaking and walking. It does not refer to the eating case.

phrases.english: It is taught about the end of the other section.
"An oath that I will not sleep,"
"that I will not speak," "that I will not walk": it is forbidden.
This is a stringency of oaths over vows.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-anchoring: the line refers to a different clause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'stringency' line compares the eating vow with the eating oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: It compares a vow and an oath on sleeping, speaking and walking.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: how vows are stricter than oaths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about how a vow can be stricter than an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says there is a stringency of vows over oaths. How so? And so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next discussion by quoting the משנה's opposite rule: sometimes a vow is stricter than an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה. A vow can forbid something even when that clashes with a מצוה, but an oath cannot. The next step looks for the source of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: A stringency of vows over oaths:
how so? etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vows are sometimes stricter than oaths.

steps.title: Source that one cannot swear to break a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל, quoting רב or שמואל, learns from 'לא יחל דברו' that an oath cannot take effect against the מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא reports this in the name of רב גידל quoting רב. רב טביומי reports it in the name of רב גידל quoting שמואל. From where do we know that one cannot swear to break the מצוות? The פסוק says 'he shall not profane his word.' Read it as: 'his word' he shall not profane, but he does profane it for the wishes of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that an oath to break a מצוה does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who said it: either רב or שמואל, both through רב גידל. The פסוק stresses 'his word', meaning a person must keep promises about his own matters. But when the oath goes against what ה׳ wants, he 'profanes' it, so the oath does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not profane (break his word)
The wishes of Heaven, meaning the מצוות

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source for the rule that a שבועה cannot override a מצוה. It sets up the difference between שבועה and נדר.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana teaches:
Rav Giddel said that Rav said.
And Rav Tavyumei teaches:
Rav Giddel said that Shmuel said.
From where do we know that one cannot swear
to break the מצוות?
The verse says: "He shall not profane his word"
"his word" he shall not profane,
phrases.notes: The גמרא flips the word order to put the stress on 'his word', meaning his own matters.

phrases.english: but he does profane it for the wishes of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין נִשְׁבָּעִין לַעֲבוֹר עַל הַמִּצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's rule quoted in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath to break a מצוה does not take effect, learned from 'דברו לא יחל'.

steps.title: Why should a vow differ, when the same פסוק covers oaths?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a נדר can override a מצוה but a שבועה cannot, since the פסוק mentions both.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a vow? Because it is written, 'When a man makes a vow to ה׳... he shall not profane his word.' But with an oath it is also written, 'or swears an oath to ה׳, he shall not profane his word'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the difference between vows and oaths. The same פסוק uses the same words for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might explain that 'a vow to ה׳' shows a vow works even on matters of ה׳, like מצוות. But that same פסוק also says 'swears an oath to ה׳', with the same 'he shall not profane his word'. So the פסוק itself seems to treat both the same. The next step, with אביי's answer, responds to this.
steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases come from the same פסוק (במדבר 30:3). That is exactly why the challenge is strong.

phrases.english: What is different about a vow?
Because it is written: "When a man makes a vow to ה׳
... he shall not profane his word."
But with an oath also, it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹ הִשָּׁבַע שְׁבֻעָה לַה׳ לֹא יַחֵל דְּבָרוֹ״!
phrases.english: "Or swears an oath to ה׳, he shall not profane his word"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference between נדר and שבועה built on step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between נדר and שבועה regarding overriding מצוות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'לה׳' and 'לא יחל דברו' appear for both vow and oath in the same פסוק, so no difference can be drawn from it.

steps.title: אביי: The Difference Is in the Wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the two cases differ in how the person worded his statement. 'The benefit of a סוכה is forbidden to me' takes effect. 'I swear I will not benefit from the סוכה' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This case is where he said 'The benefit of a סוכה is upon me [forbidden].' That case is where he said 'I swear that I will not benefit from the סוכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 5. He says the vow case and the oath case use different wording, and that is why they come out differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow wording, 'the benefit of a סוכה is on me', makes the סוכה itself forbidden to him. That kind of ban takes effect even against a מצוה. The oath wording only says what the person will not do, and a person cannot swear to hold back from a מצוה he is obligated to do.

keyTerms.meaning: This [case] ... that [case]: a way of assigning two rulings to two different situations
The booth a person must dwell in on סוכות
Upon me, meaning 'is forbidden to me' in vow language

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This [case] is where he said, 'The benefit of a sukka is upon me,'
phrases.notes: 'Upon me' is vow language meaning 'forbidden to me,' so the ban is placed on the סוכה itself.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר ״שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אֶהֱנֶה מִן הַסּוּכָּה״.
phrases.english: that [case] is where he said, 'An oath that I will not benefit from the sukka.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5 about why a נדר and a שבועה differ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the wording used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדר and a שבועה were thought to differ simply because one is a vow and the other is an oath, even though the פסוק mentions both
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference comes from the wording: banning the סוכה itself ('benefit of a סוכה on me') takes effect, while swearing off one's own action does not

steps.title: רבא: מצוות Are Not 'Benefit'
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's wording. Doing a מצוה is not considered getting benefit, so a vow against the 'benefit' of a סוכה would not stop someone from doing the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Were מצוות given for benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer. He says the word 'benefit' does not fit a מצוה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in a סוכה for the מצוה is not called 'benefit'. So if someone forbids 'the benefit of a סוכה' to himself, he never forbade the מצוה in the first place. אביי's case therefore cannot be the example of a vow that overrides a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so that...? (introduces a strong challenge)
מצוות were not given for benefit, a well-known rule

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying a person gets nothing good from מצוות. He is saying that, in הלכה, doing a מצוה does not count as 'benefit' for vows and bans.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו' appears in many places in ש״ס. It decides when doing a מצוה counts as forbidden 'benefit'.

phrases.english: Rava said:
But were מצוות given for deriving benefit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְכִי מִצְוֹת לֵיהָנוֹת נִיתְּנוּ
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of the wording 'הנאת סוכה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצוה is not 'benefit', so a vow against benefit from a סוכה does not cover the מצוה. It cannot be the case where a vow overrides a מצוה.

steps.title: רבא: The Wording Is About Sitting
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers his own version of the cases. 'Sitting in a סוכה is forbidden to me' is the vow that takes effect. 'I swear I will not sit in a סוכה' is the oath that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This case is where he said 'Sitting in a סוכה is upon me [forbidden].' That case is where he said 'I swear that I will not sit in a סוכה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps אביי's idea that the wording matters. He changes the word from 'benefit' to 'sitting', which really is the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the סוכה is exactly the act of the מצוה. So a vow placing a ban on 'sitting in a סוכה' really does clash with the מצוה, and it takes effect. The oath version, 'I will not sit', is a personal promise against a מצוה, and it does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
Sitting or dwelling, here the act of the סוכה מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא agree that a vow which bans the item ('X is forbidden to me') can override a מצוה, while an oath about one's own action cannot. They only argue about which wording shows this. רבא uses 'sitting in a סוכה' because 'benefit' does not include a מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
this [case] is where he said, 'Sitting in a sukka is upon me,'
and that [case] is where he said, 'An oath that I will not sit in a sukka.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer after רבא's challenge in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by wording, with better wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to אביי, the vow case used the word 'benefit'
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow case uses 'sitting in a סוכה', which truly covers the מצוה, so the vow takes effect against it, while the matching oath does not

steps.title: Is the Source Really This Verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the rule that an oath cannot cancel a מצוה really comes from 'לא יחל דברו' (step 4). It says the rule is learned from a different source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the rule that one cannot swear to break the מצוות learned from here? It is learned from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions רב גידל's source from step 4. It claims the rule comes from a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל learned from 'לא יחל דברו' that an oath does not take effect against a מצוה. The גמרא says this rule is already learned from another פסוק. If so, why do we need 'לא יחל דברו' for it?

keyTerms.meaning: To break or go against the מצוות
He learns it, it is derived

phrases.english: And [the rule] that one cannot take an oath to transgress the מצוות,
is it derived from here?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פסוק 'לא יחל דברו' that רב גידל used earlier.

phrases.english: It is derived from there,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאֵין נִשְׁבָּעִין לַעֲבוֹר עַל הַמִּצְוֹת מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wording discussion and goes back to question the source given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גידל's derivation from 'לא יחל דברו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that an oath cannot cancel a מצוה is learned from another source, so this פסוק seems unneeded for it

steps.title: The ברייתא Brought as the Other Source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא. It considers someone who swore to cancel a מצוה and did not cancel it, and asks whether he might be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One might think that if someone swore to cancel a מצוה and did not cancel it, he might be liable...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the ברייתא that is the 'other source' it just mentioned. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up a possible thought: someone swore to cancel a מצוה, then kept the מצוה. Maybe he should be liable for breaking his oath? The rest of the ברייתא will reject this and give the source, which is the 'מהתם' the גמרא is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
One might think (opens an idea that will be rejected)

phrases.english: as it is taught [in a baraita]:
One might think that if one swore to nullify the מצוה
and did not nullify it,
one might think he will be liable —

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל נִשְׁבַּע לְבַטֵּל אֶת הַמִּצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the claim 'מהתם נפקא ליה' in step 9
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the rule against swearing to break מצוות is learned from a different source
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about someone who swore to cancel a מצוה and did not cancel it
